results.label: this tree ships the M110 news-window module (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
the policy names TWO settings with distinct bounds and says a single knob does not exist
the pre-release default is 15 and the post-release default is 45
the settle floor is 30 minutes and the block floor is 1
the recommendation is labelled a recommendation, not a floor, for the block
the doctrine is quoted (15 default, "at least 15", the 30–60 settle, the 5/10/30/60 options)
the basis states the two clocks, labels the numbers as recommendations and names the one enforced floor
the module exports no write path at all
both settings are accepted at their bounds (block 60, settle 30)
the values he demonstrates are all storable: 5, 10, 15, 30, 60
a settle below the 30-minute floor is REFUSED, not silently stored, and says why
the refusal message says the two sides are separate, so shortening one cannot shorten the other
the old single knob is REFUSED with its own code rather than split for the caller
hostile shapes are refused: true, arrays, objects, blanks, 1.5, 0, 241, 1e9
a string integer is accepted as that integer, the way the app already reads numeric settings
a block below 15 is stored WITH a named warning quoting his recommendation
that warning does not touch the settle: the other side is unchanged by it
a row stored below the settle floor is CLAMPED UP to 30 on read, never used as stored
a row stored below the block minimum is clamped to 1 and both clamps are reported by field
each clamp names the stored value, the value used and the reason
a missing/legacy row falls back to the episode defaults 15/45 and says so in its sources
an unreadable stored value falls back to the default and is reported as a clamp, not guessed
a stored value above the maximum is clamped down to 240 on both sides
a per-request research pair is honoured only inside the same bounds
a release 46–100 minutes in the past is CLEAR (outside the 45-minute settle)
a release 1–45 minutes in the past is BLOCKED, on the after side, with the settle window
a release due in 1–15 minutes is BLOCKED on the before side with the 15-minute block
a release due in 16–100 minutes is CLEAR — the block is 15, not 45
the moment of the release counts as blocked, on the before side
the boundary is inclusive on both sides (exactly 15 before and exactly 45 after)
a 5-minute block does NOT shorten the settle: a release 50 minutes ago is still blocked
and the same 5-minute block does not stretch the before side: 6 minutes ahead is clear
the recorded failure is now impossible: no plan can produce a 5-minute settle
an unparseable date is not a hit and not a miss dressed up as a hit
bots/index.js applies the pair through hit() and has no absolute-difference window test left in code
bots/index.js has no windowMin identifier left in code (the comment quoting the old line is not a live test)
the news check refuses a bare number for both sides and says so
the owner module keeps the asymmetric comparison in exactly one exported function and uses no absolute distance
the module documents that M111 (calendar failure) is NOT solved here
the same stored row produces the same pair twice (deterministic, no clock, no randomness)
the detail note interpolates the CONFIGURED numbers, so it cannot describe a window the app is not applying

scope: M110 module: two clocks, bounds, refusal of the single knob, clamp on read, asymmetry: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock and a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser; two asymmetric news clocks, no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
